A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GUARD study. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original lexical-constraint and sentiment-reversal experiments, diversity analyses, and appendix comparisons of IMH and QRS.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds an evaluated heuristic keyword-enforcement sampler in Appendix E.

M1.justification: GUARD retains the same CAP, SFT, and DPG proposal options, warm-start training, and rejection sampler. Moving policy initialization outside Algorithm 2's optional CAP block clarifies initialization already described in v1 rather than introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate lexical inclusion, including the additional restaurant/world positional analyses, and ROCStories completion with positive endings. The new heuristic uses the existing 30-token amazing task. CommonGen is newly discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix E adds an evaluated heuristic that forces amazing at the final token if absent earlier, comparing its divergence with existing DPG/SFT results. Other comparator sets remain unchanged; the newly discussed HMM approaches and NADO are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Evaluation models, training budgets, thresholds, metrics, and hyperparameters in Tables 3 and 6 remain unchanged. The heuristic comparison uses the existing lexical setting. Appendix D newly discloses evaluation sampling details without reporting a revision to the existing protocol.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix E adds an empirical check of whether heuristic keyword enforcement preserves the gold distribution, supporting the discussion of positional distortion. Existing diversity, positional-bias, generated-example, and IMH/QRS analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2 explains the existing KL estimator and discloses its sample size without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds the heuristic sampler's KL divergence of 6.06, compared with 0.633 for the existing warm-start DPG result. Retained plots, diversity scores, and IMH/QRS findings are unchanged. Explicit acceptance rates of 0.416 and 0.306 clarify the previously reported approximately 180-fold and 60-fold improvements.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.7 derives the SFT/DPG KL objectives and gradient, while B.1 adds a probability-ratio preservation property. PTC and P≠NP become explicit in theorem statements, although already present in v1's appendix and proof reasoning. Core proofs remain intact; B.7 introduces a sign slip in the entropy constant.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same gold-distribution objective, autoregressive limitation, GUARD guarantees, and efficiency claims. Explicitly identifying rejection sampling from the base LLM as the efficiency comparator clarifies the existing claim.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix B.1 interprets probability-ratio preservation as preserving knowledge and reasoning over constraint-satisfying outputs. Section 4 explicitly distinguishes distributional evaluation from downstream benchmark performance. The existing limitation concerning inaccurate constraint filters remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code release; v2 supplies a repository link. Appendix D newly documents KL estimation using 2^20 base-model samples, yielding approximately 2,300 lexical and 5,000 sentiment samples after filtering. These are added reproducibility details, not evidence of rerun experiments.

R1.justification: Section 5 replaces the blanket assertion that controlled-generation methods cannot enforce strict constraints with acknowledgment of HMM-based guarantees. New Appendix A substantially compares Zhang et al.'s approaches and NADO with GUARD, distinguishing arbitrary predicates, distributional fidelity, and sampling efficiency. Additional citations broaden coverage of guided decoding.

P1.justification: Localized revisions clarify terminology and theorem assumptions, expand related-work and optimization explanations, and update affiliations and acknowledgments. The main section order and most existing prose remain intact; the appendices are extended and renumbered.

P2.justification: Existing figures are relocated and renumbered, diversity tables are widened, appendix tables are resized, and Algorithm 2 becomes a single-column display. Algorithm 1's display disappears despite retained references, although its procedure remains in prose. No new result plots are added.

improvement.justification: v2 improves research positioning through qualified comparisons with other strict-constraint methods, and improves assessability through the heuristic control, explicit theorem assumptions, KL sampling details, and code access information. These are limited gains around unchanged main results. They outweigh the missing Algorithm 1 display and the new entropy-sign slip, which does not change the derived gradient.
